correctness.rationale: For every n>=3, independently proved exact power-domination feasibility from the initial unobserved rectangle U x W. Minimum sets are exactly row or column near-transversals. The induced row/column slide graphs each have degree n(n-1), their overlap has degree 2(n-1), and no cross-family slide bypasses their intersection, yielding the exact edge formula. An explicit two-coordinate slide strategy gives distance <=2(n-1) for all pairs; if any coordinate is shared it saves a move, while same-family pairs need at most n moves. Hence only the specified n^2 opposite row-column star pairs can attain the bound; the two-coordinate demand per token proves each requires at least 2(n-1). Independently implemented code directly checks power-domination closure and bitmask-based state graphs at n=3,4,5; all-pairs distances at n=3,4 and selected BFS at n=5 agree. Finite code is supporting evidence, not the all-order proof.

value.rationale: A natural optimal sensor movement problem is solved for every square rook graph, not a handpicked numerical instance. The theorem shows that all minimum-size monitoring placements remain connected under physical graph-edge moves, but the sharp worst-case effort grows linearly as 2n-2 even though a single rook-graph vertex has diameter two. Its n^2 diameter pairs have an intrinsic, exactly characterized geometry (opposite missing-row/missing-column star configurations). The number of legal slides is also exact. These conclusions are not simple consequences of the known minimum-set count, and furnish a structural benchmark for constrained relocation without spare sensors.
